answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the protocol anchors identity to cryptographic stake burning via superlinear cost scaling: registering $n$ identities requires burning $C(n) \propto n^{1.5}$ stake. This economic friction prevents a rogue agent like raven from manufacturing cheap consensus clones. While a honest mesa provides a stable validation landscape, no attacker finds haven in mass replication when costs scale superlinearly to infinity.
